title: Push as Two Tape Actions
statement: Let $c$ be a partial recursive program, let $x$ be a finite input string over the bridge alphabet, and let $q,q_m,q'$ be optional control states of its bridging machine. Given a valid input-head position $p$, an assignment $st$ of compiled-machine stacks, an output string, a stack name $k$, and a compiled-stack symbol $a$, perform two actions on the work tape corresponding to $k$: first move its head one cell left without writing, then write $a$ (embedded in the bridge alphabet) without moving. The resulting configuration has control state $q'$, input position $p$, unchanged output, and stack assignment obtained by replacing $st(k)$ with $a$ prepended to it; the intermediate state is $q_m$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite input string over the bridge alphabet
replaced:
Pushing a symbol $a$ onto the stack named $k$ is realized by two consecutive
one-tape actions on the tape of $k$: first move that head one cell to the left
(writing nothing), then write the embedded symbol $a$ without moving.  Applied to a
bridge configuration, this yields the bridge configuration whose assignment replaces
the stack at $k$ by $a$ prepended to it, with the specified final control state and
the input position and output unchanged.
